name: gemini_ask
description:
Ask Gemini a question or give it a reading task, through the Antigravity
CLI on the user's Google AI Pro plan (no API cost; uses the plan's limits).

Good for a second opinion on code or a design, reviewing local files passed
in `paths`, and long reasoning. The text of each file up to 20 000
characters goes into the prompt, so pass the files themselves; Gemini
can't open folders or larger files on its own when the Antigravity CLI
runs headless. Gemini runs read-only: it can search the web but cannot
change files or run commands. For web research with cited sources use
gemini_research; to let Gemini edit a folder use gemini_code.

Args:
    prompt: The question or task.
    model: Model id from gemini_models (e.g. "gemini-3.8-flash-medium");
        default is agy's (or GEMINI_PRO_AGY_MODEL).
    paths: Local files for Gemini to read; their text is sent with the
        prompt (about 22 000 characters in all).
    conversation_id: Continue an earlier gemini_ask/gemini_research chat.
    effort: Reasoning effort: low, medium, high, xhigh or max.

Returns:
    Gemini's answer and a conversation_id for follow-ups.

name: gemini_research
description:
Research a question on the live web with Gemini and Google Search, and
get an answer that cites its sources. Use it for current facts, releases,
prices, docs or comparisons that may be newer than your training data.

Runs through the Antigravity CLI on the user's Google AI Pro plan: no API
cost, uses the plan's limits. Read-only. Gemini prefers official sources,
cross-checks key facts and says when sources disagree. Usually takes one
to three minutes. For questions about local files use gemini_ask instead.

Args:
    question: What to find out, with context that narrows it, e.g.
        "What changed in Flutter 3.47 for Android builds?".
    model: Model id from gemini_models, e.g. "gemini-4-argon-high";
        omit for agy's default (or GEMINI_PRO_AGY_MODEL).
    effort: Reasoning effort: "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh" or "max".

Returns:
    The answer followed by a "Sources" list of URLs, and a conversation_id;
    pass it to gemini_ask to ask follow-up questions in the same chat.

name: gemini_code
description:
Delegate a coding task to Gemini, which reads and EDITS files in one
local folder through the Antigravity agent on the user's Google AI Pro plan
(no API cost). This changes files: tell the user, and review the result
afterwards, e.g. with `git diff`. Gemini can't run terminal commands here,
so run the tests yourself afterwards. Antigravity CLI 1.5 can't get approval
for file access when it runs headless. Then this tool returns agy's
explanation within about a minute and changes nothing; use jules_start
instead.

Good for a well-defined change: fix a bug, add tests, refactor a module.
For read-only questions use gemini_ask; for a task on a GitHub repo that
should end in a pull request use jules_start.

Args:
    task: What to change and how to know it is done, e.g. "Add unit tests
        for parse_date in utils/dates.py; all tests must pass".
    folder: Absolute path of the project folder Gemini may edit.
    model: Model id from gemini_models; omit for agy's default.
    agent: Name of an Antigravity agent from gemini_agents to run the task.
    effort: Reasoning effort: "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh" or "max".
    conversation_id: Continue an earlier gemini_code or gemini_ask chat, e.g.
        to ask for fixes to the previous change.

Returns:
    Gemini's summary of what it changed, and a conversation_id for follow-up
    requests; or an error if the folder does not exist.

name: gemini_agents
description:
List the custom Antigravity agents the user has made or installed, such
as a "reviewer" or "test-writer" agent with its own instructions.
Read-only, free and quick. Call it before gemini_code when the user wants
a task done by a specific agent.

Returns:
    The agent names and descriptions as the Antigravity CLI prints them; pass
    a name as `agent` to gemini_code. "No custom agents." if there are none.

name: gemini_models
description:
List the models the user's Google account can use through the Antigravity
CLI, e.g. Gemini 4 Argon and Gemini 3.8 Flash at several thinking levels.
Read-only, free and quick. Call it when the user asks for a specific or
stronger model; otherwise the gemini_* tools use agy's default.

Returns:
    One "id — name" line per model, e.g. "gemini-4-argon-high — Gemini 4
    Argon (High)". Pass the id as `model` to gemini_ask, gemini_research or
    gemini_code.

name: video_generate
description:
Generate a short video with native sound from a text prompt, with Gemini
Omni Flash through the Gemini API, and save it as an .mp4 in
GEMINI_PRO_OUTPUT_DIR. One call makes one clip of about 8 seconds; for
longer videos chain video_edit, or use flow_make_video on the user's Flow
credits when browser tools are enabled.

COSTS MONEY: billed to the API key's Google Cloud project (about $0.10 per
second of 720p video, no free tier). Confirm with the user before calling.

Args:
    prompt: Subject, action, setting, camera and sound, e.g. "A red tram
        crosses Baku at sunset, slow dolly shot, street noise". English works
        best; timecodes like "[0-3s] ... [3-6s] ..." sequence the shot.
    aspect_ratio: "16:9" (landscape, default) or "9:16" (vertical).
    resolution: "720p" (default), "360p", or upscaled "1080p" or "4k".
    first_frame: Local image path the video starts from.
    last_frame: Local image path the video ends on.
    reference_images: Up to 3 local images of characters or objects to keep.
    file_name: Optional .mp4 file name; default is the date plus prompt words.
    wait_seconds: How long to wait for the render (default 300) before
        returning an id to fetch later with video_check.

Returns:
    The saved .mp4 path and an id to change or extend it with video_edit;
    or, if rendering takes longer than wait_seconds, an id for video_check.

name: video_edit
description:
Change or extend a video; the result is saved as a new file.

COSTS MONEY: billed like video_generate. Confirm with the user before calling.
Give exactly one of previous_id (from video_generate/video_edit) or
video_path (a local video of 10 seconds or less).

Args:
    instruction: e.g. "Make it night", or to extend: "Continue the scene:
        the car drives off" (adds 3-10 s, up to 40 s in total).
    previous_id: id returned by an earlier video_generate or video_edit.
    video_path: Local video (max 10 s) to edit instead.
    aspect_ratio: "16:9" or "9:16".
    resolution: "720p" (default), "360p", "1080p" or "4k".
    file_name: Optional .mp4 file name.
    wait_seconds: How long to wait before returning an id for video_check.

Returns:
    The saved .mp4 path and a new id (or an id for video_check).

name: video_check
description:
Fetch a video that video_generate or video_edit started but had not
finished rendering when they returned, and save it as an .mp4. Free: the
video was paid for when it was started, and checking costs nothing. Call it
again with the same id if the video is still rendering.

Args:
    id: The id returned by video_generate or video_edit.
    wait_seconds: How long to keep waiting in this call (default 120)
        before returning the current status.

Returns:
    The saved .mp4 path and an id for video_edit once the video is ready;
    otherwise its status (still rendering, or failed with the reason).

name: image_generate
description:
Create a new image from a prompt, or edit local images, with Nano Banana
through the Gemini API, and save the result in GEMINI_PRO_OUTPUT_DIR. Pass
previous_id to refine an earlier result step by step ("make the sky
darker") without starting over.

COSTS MONEY: about $0.034 (1K), $0.05 (2K) or $0.11 (4K) per image with
Nano Banana 2.1; Nano Banana Pro ("gemini-3-pro-image") is $0.13-0.24.
No free tier. Confirm with the user before calling.

Args:
    prompt: What to draw, or how to change the input images, e.g. "Turn
        this sketch into a clean flat app icon on a white background".
    model: "gemini-nano-banana-2.1" (default), "gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image"
        (cheapest, 1K only) or "gemini-3-pro-image" (best, for hard tasks).
    aspect_ratio: "1:1" (default), "2:3", "3:2", "3:4", "4:3", "4:5", "5:4",
        "9:16", "16:9" or "21:9".
    image_size: "1K" (default), "2K" or "4K".
    input_images: Local image paths to edit or to use as references.
    previous_id: The id of an earlier image_generate result to refine.
    file_name: Optional file name; default is the date plus prompt words.

Returns:
    The saved image path and an id to pass as previous_id for further edits.

name: video_stitch
description:
Join local video clips, in the given order, into one .mp4 with ffmpeg.
Runs on this computer and costs nothing. Clips with the same format (e.g.
all from video_generate or Flow) are joined losslessly; mixed formats are
re-encoded to H.264/AAC. Use it to combine clips made by video_generate,
video_edit or flow_collect; flow_make_video already joins its own clips.

Args:
    clips: Paths of the clips, first to last (at least one).
    file_name: Name for the joined file, saved in GEMINI_PRO_OUTPUT_DIR; a
        number is added if it already exists.

Returns:
    "Saved: <path>" with the joined video, or an error such as a missing clip.

name: jules_sources
description:
List the GitHub repositories the user has connected to Jules, Google's
cloud coding agent. Read-only and free. Call it before jules_start to get
the exact repo name; Jules can only work on repositories listed here.

Returns:
    One source name per line, e.g. "github/owner/repo", to pass as `repo`
    to jules_start; or a note that no repository is connected yet, with the
    link where the user connects GitHub.

name: jules_start
description:
Start a Jules session: Google's coding agent works on a task in one of
the user's GitHub repositories, in the cloud and asynchronously, within the
Google AI Pro plan's Jules limits (no extra cost). It can push a branch and
open a pull request, so confirm the task with the user first.

Then poll with jules_status, answer questions with jules_message, and
approve the plan with jules_approve_plan if you asked for approval. For a
change in a local folder use gemini_code instead.

Args:
    prompt: The task with acceptance criteria, e.g. "Add input validation
        to the /signup endpoint and tests for it".
    repo: Repository from jules_sources, e.g. "github/owner/repo"; omit for
        a session without a repository.
    branch: Branch Jules starts from (default "main").
    title: Optional session title; Jules makes one up otherwise.
    create_pr: True lets Jules open a pull request automatically when done.
    require_plan_approval: True makes Jules wait for jules_approve_plan
        before it changes any code.

Returns:
    The session id and its web link (https://jules.google.com/session/<id>),
    or an error such as an unknown repository.

name: jules_status
description:
Check on a Jules session started with jules_start: its state, its most
recent activities (plan, progress messages, questions, completion) and the
pull request it opened, if any. Read-only and free; call it again to poll a
session that is still working.

Use jules_sessions to find a session id, jules_approve_plan when the state
says it awaits plan approval, and jules_message to answer a question.

Args:
    session: Session id from jules_start or jules_sessions, or its full
        "sessions/<id>" name or web link.
    activities: How many of the latest activities to show (default 15).

Returns:
    The session title and state, any pull request links, and one line per
    recent activity with its time, kind and text.

name: jules_sessions
description:
List the user's most recent Jules sessions, newest first, to find a
session id or see which tasks are still running. Read-only and free.

Pass an id from the result to jules_status for details, to
jules_approve_plan or to jules_message.

Args:
    limit: How many sessions to list (default 10).

Returns:
    One line per session: id, state (as Jules reports it, for example in
    progress, awaiting plan approval or completed) and title, or
    "No sessions yet."

name: jules_approve_plan
description:
Approve the plan Jules proposed, so it starts writing code. Only for a
session started with jules_start(require_plan_approval=True) whose state is
awaiting plan approval; read the plan with jules_status first and show it
to the user. To change the plan instead, send feedback with jules_message.

Args:
    session: Session id from jules_start or jules_sessions.

Returns:
    A confirmation that Jules is working, or an error such as the session
    not waiting for approval. Follow progress with jules_status.

name: jules_message
description:
Send a message to Jules inside an existing session: answer a question it
asked, give feedback on its plan or code, or ask for a change. Jules
replies asynchronously, so read the answer later with jules_status. To give
Jules a new task, use jules_start instead.

Args:
    session: Session id from jules_start or jules_sessions.
    message: What to tell Jules, in plain language.

Returns:
    A confirmation that the message was sent, or an error.

name: google_pro_benefits
description:
List everything a Google AI Pro plan includes and which tool of this
server reaches each part, or why a part cannot be reached (mobile-only,
US-only, purchases). Read-only, free and offline. Call it first when the
user asks what their plan can do or which tool to use.

The browser-based tools it names (Flow, Gemini app, Notebooks, AI Mode)
appear only when the server runs with GEMINI_PRO_ENABLE_BROWSER=1.

Returns:
    One entry per benefit: what it is, where it lives, and how to use it here.
